questionText: Which particle in an atom carries a negative charge?
explanation: Protons are positive, neutrons are neutral, and electrons are the negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus.

questionText: Which of these best describes an ionic bond?

options.text: Atoms share a pair of electrons
One atom transfers electrons to another, forming oppositely charged ions that attract
Atoms exchange neutrons to become stable

explanation: Ionic bonding involves electron transfer (not sharing) between atoms, creating a positive ion and a negative ion that are held together by electrostatic attraction.

questionText: One mole of any substance contains the same number of particles. What is this number called?
explanation: Avogadro's number (about 6.022 × 10^23) is the number of particles in exactly one mole of a substance.

questionText: Molarity (concentration in mol/L) is calculated as moles of solute divided by what?

options.text: The mass of the solvent in kilograms
The volume of the solution in litres
The volume of solvent added, before mixing

explanation: Molarity = moles of solute ÷ volume of the final solution (in litres) — not the solvent alone, since the solute itself adds to the total volume.

questionText: Which of these correctly orders three metals from most reactive to least reactive?
explanation: In the reactivity series, potassium (a group 1 metal) is far more reactive than zinc, which in turn is more reactive than copper — copper is one of the least reactive common metals.

questionText: In an exothermic reaction, energy is...
explanation: Exo- means 'out' — an exothermic reaction releases energy (usually as heat) to the surroundings, so the surroundings get warmer.

questionText: Activation energy is best described as...

options.text: The total energy released by a reaction
The minimum energy needed to get a reaction started
The total energy stored in the products

explanation: Activation energy is the energy 'barrier' that reactants must overcome before a reaction can proceed, regardless of whether the overall reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

The total mass of the reactants

explanation: Entropy (S) measures disorder — a gas has higher entropy than a liquid, which has higher entropy than a solid, because particles are more randomly arranged.
